paa_questions.question: What are the basics of BJJ for beginners?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: BJJ basics include five core concepts (base, posture, frames, leverage, weight distribution) and five fundamental positions (closed guard, mount, side control, back control, standing). White belts should prioritize escapes and defensive awareness before developing offensive attacks.
paa_questions.rationale: Highest-volume beginner BJJ query — the article covers this perfectly but the opening heading should front-load this answer

paa_questions.question: How long does it take to learn BJJ fundamentals?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Most practitioners develop solid fundamentals over 18-36 months (white to blue belt). Core concepts — base, posture, frames — typically click within 6 months with consistent 2-3x/week training. Full systematic integration takes until purple belt (3-5 years).
paa_questions.rationale: Extremely high-volume query from prospective students; article has the belt progression framework but no direct answer to 'how long' — add a FAQ callout

paa_questions.question: What is the best way to learn BJJ at home?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: At home, use visual learning tools (position maps, technique videos, knowledge graphs) to understand position relationships. Supplement with solo drills (hip escapes, shrimping, bridging) and conceptual study (decision trees, position hierarchy). Live training cannot be fully replaced but conceptual gaps can be filled.
paa_questions.rationale: High-volume query that maps directly to BJJ Graph's value proposition — add a dedicated 'How to Use This Visual System at Home' section

paa_questions.question: What BJJ techniques should a white belt learn first?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Priority order: (1) mount escape, (2) side control escape, (3) closed guard maintenance, (4) basic closed guard sweeps (hip bump, scissor), (5) guard pass from knees. Master escapes before attacks — you spend more time defending as a white belt.
paa_questions.rationale: Most common white belt question; the article covers this in the 'White Belt' section but not as a directly answerable snippet — restructure as numbered FAQ

paa_questions.question: What is position before submission in BJJ?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: 'Position before submission' means securing dominant positions (mount, back control, side control) before attempting submissions. Abandoning a dominant position to chase a submission risks losing advantage. The principle reflects that 4-point positions create submission opportunities naturally.
paa_questions.rationale: Core BJJ principle query with high informational intent — article mentions it in passing; add a dedicated FAQ paragraph for featured snippet capture

paa_questions.question: How do BJJ belts work?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: BJJ adult belts progress: White → Blue → Purple → Brown → Black. Each rank represents years of training and demonstrated skill. White (0-2 years), Blue (2-4 years), Purple (4-7 years), Brown (7-9 years), Black (9+ years). Coral and red belts are senior/grandmaster ranks.
paa_questions.rationale: High-volume query from beginners; article covers white-to-purple progression but not the full belt system — add a brief belt system overview

paa_questions.question: What is base in BJJ?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Base in BJJ is the stability created by your contact points with the ground (feet, knees, hips, hands). Good base requires a wide stance, low center of gravity, multiple ground contacts, and dynamic balance to resist sweeps and reversals.
paa_questions.rationale: Definition query that article answers well — heading 'Base: The Foundation of Stability' is good but adding a direct one-sentence definition at the top of the section improves snippet eligibility

paa_questions.question: Is BJJ effective in a real fight?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: BJJ is highly effective in real fights because over 90% of street altercations go to the ground. BJJ ground control, submissions, and positional dominance allow smaller practitioners to neutralize larger attackers. The systematic positional hierarchy teaches safe engagement and disengagement.
paa_questions.rationale: High self-defense intent traffic; article doesn't address this — a brief self-defense applicability section broadens audience capture

paa_questions.question: How many times a week should a BJJ beginner train?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: BJJ beginners should train 2-3 times per week consistently. Below 2 sessions/week, muscle memory and conditioning develop too slowly. Above 4 sessions/week, recovery becomes a limiting factor for beginners. Consistency over months matters more than training frequency.
paa_questions.rationale: High-volume practical query from new students; article mentions '2-3 sessions per week' but doesn't explain why — add an FAQ explanation

paa_questions.question: What is the difference between BJJ and wrestling?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: BJJ focuses on ground fighting, submissions (chokes, joint locks), and positional control. Wrestling emphasizes takedowns, throws, and pins. BJJ allows defeating a larger opponent via submissions; wrestling uses athleticism and scrambling. Many grapplers combine both.
paa_questions.rationale: Cross-sport comparison query with moderate volume; a brief differentiation note helps the article rank for comparison queries
